c.tagline: Lakeside Rwandan border town on Lake Kivu, gateway to Nyungwe's chimps and canopy walk.

taxi.fareNote: There are no ride-hailing apps or metered taxis in Cyangugu/Kamembe; red-vested moto-taxis are the main way around town (helmet provided) and shared minibuses run fixed routes. Agree the moto fare before you set off.

emergency.note: 112 reaches police and general emergencies while 912 is the ambulance/SAMU line; Rwanda is very safe but medical facilities near the DRC border are basic, with serious cases referred to Kigali.

avoid.reason: Do not cross into or linger along the DR Congo border with Bukavu, where conflict in eastern DRC makes the frontier zone volatile.
Petty theft can occur around the border crossing, market and bus park; keep documents secure amid border crowds.

hood_desc: The low-density older quarter strung along the southern shore of Lake Kivu right at the DRC frontier, facing Bukavu across the Ruzizi River; quiet, scenic lodgings and the border bridge make this the calm, view-filled base.

The higher-density commercial and transport hub inland from the lake, home to the market, banks, bus park and Kamembe Airport; the practical, central place to stay for onward travel to Nyungwe or Kigali.
A residential area of Kamembe known for its schools and churches on the slopes above town; local, green and quiet, suiting travelers who want an everyday-Rwanda feel away from the border bustle.
The sector at the Ruzizi I crossing where Rwanda meets Bukavu, with the border market, tea-country roads and lakeside views; a workaday frontier zone rather than a tourist strip.
Rwanda's inhabited island in Lake Kivu reached by boat from Cyangugu, with fishing villages, pottery and birdlife; a rustic, off-grid escape for travelers wanting local island life.

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water; tap water is not reliably potable.

transit.pay: Moto-taxi and minibus fares are paid in cash (Rwandan francs) or increasingly via mobile money; agree the moto fare before setting off. There is no transit card in Cyangugu.
transit.hours: Moto-taxis and minibuses run roughly 6:00 AM to 9:00 PM; motos are the main after-dark option.
transit.note: Cyangugu/Kamembe has no rail or city-bus network. Helmeted red-vested moto-taxis are the backbone of local transport, supplemented by shared minibuses on fixed routes and long-distance coaches to Kigali.

bus: Long-distance coaches (Volcano, Ritco) to Kigali via Nyungwe or Huye
ferry: Lake Kivu boats north toward Karongi (Kibuye) and Rubavu

transit.m: Taxi to Kamembe / Cyangugu centre (10-15 min)

tip.r: Not customary; a 5-10% tip for good service at tourist lodges and for park and forest guides is appreciated but not expected.
